title: Florian Wirtz Reveals Why Germany Easily Scored Against the Netherlands – Bavarian Football Works
body:
Germany’s 5‑0 demolition of the Netherlands in Düsseldorf on Tuesday left many pundits scrambling for an explanation, and midfielder Florian Wirtz was quick to point to the influence of Jürgen Klopp’s coaching philosophy as the decisive factor. The 22‑year‑old, who has become a linchpin in the German side’s attacking trident, described how the German manager’s high‑pressing, freedom‑focused system created an environment in which the team could exploit the Dutch defensive frailties with almost surgical precision. The result, Wirtz said, was a “perfect storm” of tactical clarity, collective confidence and individual brilliance that turned a potentially tight contest into a rout.

Klopp’s tenure with the national team, though still in its infancy, has already begun to reshape Germany’s identity on the pitch. Departing from the rigid, possession‑heavy structures that dominated the previous decade, the German coach has introduced a more aggressive, vertical style that emphasizes quick transitions and relentless pressing. This shift was evident from the opening whistle: Germany’s forwards surged forward, compressing the space between the lines and forcing the Dutch backline into uncomfortable positions. Wirtz highlighted that the “intensity we were trained to maintain from the first minute” left the Netherlands scrambling to regain composure, ultimately leading to a cascade of errors that the Germans capitalised on.

Beyond the tactical overhaul, Wirtz underscored the psychological uplift that Klopp’s man‑management brings. The German captain, Joshua Kimmich, and the young attacking duo of Wirtz and Jamal Musiala have spoken repeatedly about the freedom they feel to express themselves within a clear framework. “You know exactly what we have to do, but you also have the space to improvise,” Wirtz said. This balance between structure and liberty appears to have resonated particularly well with the younger cohort, who thrive on creative freedom. The result was a fluid attacking display, with Musiala’s dribbling opening channels, Kimmich’s incisive passing dictating tempo, and Wirtz’s late runs culminating in two of the five goals.

The Dutch side, historically known for technical finesse and positional play, seemed unprepared for the relentless German press. Their midfield failed to retain possession under pressure, and the back four was repeatedly exposed by swift diagonal balls that bypassed their central defenders. Wirtz noted that “the Dutch tried to play their usual possession game, but we forced them into a different rhythm.” By dictating the tempo, Germany effectively nullified the Netherlands’ traditional strengths, turning the match into a showcase of how modern pressing can dominate even technically adept opponents.

While the victory will boost Germany’s confidence ahead of upcoming Euro qualifiers, it also raises questions about the sustainability of such high‑intensity tactics over a long tournament. Klopp’s approach demands peak physical conditioning and mental sharpness; any dip could expose defensive vulnerabilities. Moreover, opponents will now have more footage to study, potentially devising counter‑strategies that disrupt Germany’s press. Nonetheless, Wirtz’s assessment suggests that the squad’s depth and adaptability give them a buffer against such challenges. “We have a group that believes in the system and trusts each other,” he affirmed, hinting at a collective resilience that could weather tactical adjustments from rivals.

Looking forward, Germany’s next fixtures will test whether the blueprint that produced a five‑goal masterclass can be replicated against more disciplined teams. If Klopp can maintain the balance of intensity and creative freedom that Wirtz praised, the German side may well emerge as the benchmark for modern, press‑oriented football in Europe. For now, the emphatic win serves as both a statement of intent and a reminder that under Klopp’s stewardship, Germany’s footballing renaissance is well underway.
